correctness.rationale: The left and right truncated squares force a node on each open side. If a side has one node, the ratio of its cubic and quadratic truncated moments forces its location and weight (s/4,16s/27 on the left); two nodes then carry only 16/27 of the mass. With one left node removed the two remaining nodes must be the roots of the unique monic quadratic determined by the two residual orthogonality equations; its recurrence and the two stated weights give all four residual moments. The residual determinant is -q/324 > 0 for 0<s≤1/2, and the stated discriminant is strictly positive. The residual mean is between the roots and strictly between s and 1, so the signs of the quadratic at s and 1 locate both roots in (s,1), except that the smaller root equals s at the midpoint. This also gives positivity. In the opposite pattern, reflection reduces to t>1/2; either the determinant is nonpositive or P(t)<0, excluding two positive distinct nodes both strictly right of t. A node at the knot forces the two outer rules and gives first moment (s+4)/9, hence s=1/2. The midpoint endpoint tests exclude both off-knot patterns there. For an independent derivative calculation, write P(s)=(s-r2)(s-r3)=g(s)(2s-1), g=9(1-s)^4/(2q); at 1/2, g=-9/176 and g'/g=-38/11. The derivative of the root sum u is 43/44, giving r2'=8/11 and r3'=1/4; differentiating this product twice gives r2''=96/121. The mass and first-moment equations give w2'=0, w3'=-16/27 from the left; reflection matches the complete first-derivative vector and negates the middle-node second derivative. The formula's nu is the rational coefficient defined as u, as fixed by the residual equations. In the basis explanation use the sum of the two truncated squares and the difference of the truncated cubes; these are editorial slips, not changes of the claim.
